Convert MIDI to MP3

What this does

A MIDI file stores notes and instrument programs — no sound. Making an MP3 means rendering it through a sound bank. This converter renders with the General MIDI FluidR3 soundfont in your browser, which is why a piano track plays as a GM piano rather than your DAW's sampled piano.

Open the converter with the format selected

How to convert

  1. Choose a .mid, .midi or .kar file.
  2. Set the output to MP3.
  3. Convert, then Download.

What you get

All tracks are mixed into one stereo MP3. The sound is determined by General MIDI program numbers. If the original file depends on custom instruments, the result will sound different from what you hear in your DAW.

FAQ

Why does it sound different from my DAW?

The render uses the General MIDI FluidR3 soundfont. Any custom instrument in the original arrangement is replaced by the matching GM preset.

Are all tracks mixed together?

Yes — the output is one mixed audio file, not a stem export.

Does it accept .kar files?

Yes, .kar (MIDI karaoke) files are accepted; the lyrics are not rendered into the audio.
